recentItems.title: 1681st day of hell: Zelenskyy on the front line, Baltic nuclear ultimatum, and PACE tribunal
recentItems.description:
On the Day of Defenders of Ukraine, Zelenskyy addressed the military from the front line and honored the memory of the fallen. Meanwhile, a Russian drone attacked a school in Kyiv: over 100 students and about 60 staff members were in the shelter. In Strasbourg, PACE paid tribute to Viktoria Roshchyna and other journalists killed due to Russian aggression, calling for the release of media workers from captivity. Latvia considers the deployment of nuclear weapons based on a collective NATO decision, although no negotiations are taking place yet.

recentItems.title: The DESTINY of Europe is DECIDED HERE! Zelenskyy on DEFENDERS’ DAY at the front
recentItems.description:
On the Day of Defenders and Defendresses of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy recorded an address not among capital symbols, but directly on the frontline. The President emphasized: it is precisely among camouflage nets, military positions, and command posts that the history of Ukraine is being written today and the fate of its independence is being decided.

The Head of State remembered the fallen heroes and the words of warrior and poet Maksym Kryvtsov: “When they ask me what war is, I will answer without hesitation: names.” On the 1,681st day of the full-scale war, Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked everyone defending the country — from infantrymen and artillerymen to pilots, drone operators, intelligence officers, and engineers.

The President of Ukraine is convinced that the path to peace lies precisely through the resilience of the people holding the frontline today.

This video is about those who “carry Ukraine's Independence on their shoulders,” and the price Ukraine pays for the right to remain itself.

recentItems.title: A Russian Tu-95 crashed during take-off — aircraft and killer crew lost
recentItems.description:
A Tu-95 strategic bomber has crashed in Russia’s Amur Oblast, killing six crew members. Meanwhile, Ukraine receives a powerful boost: Belgium is set to deliver three more F-16 fighter jets by the end of the year, while the UK announces a £100 million military package featuring Patriot missiles, artillery, and drones.

Also in this episode: drone strikes on the Belgorod region and severe gasoline shortages at gas stations near Moscow. The EU prepares to designate the GRU as a terrorist organization following a wave of Russian sabotage across Europe. Despite Kremlin threats, allies stress that pressure on Russia will only continue to rise.

recentItems.title: Ukraine seizes the initiative! Bold flanking attacks have forced the occupiers to flee
recentItems.description:
The Armed Forces of Ukraine are seizing the initiative in key sectors of the front, while Russia scrambles to find reserves to sustain the war. Military expert Pavlo Lakiychuk analyzes Operation "Vivaldi," counterattacks in the Lyman direction, and the situation near Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and Kupyansk. This episode also highlights an innovative Ukrainian amphibious robot that delivered supplies across land and water, as well as the air-dropping of ground robots from heavy drones. Why is the Kremlin deploying North Korean troops and shifting combat drone production to the DPRK? How are heavy Russian losses and deep precision strikes impacting Moscow’s plans? We break down the changing dynamics on the battlefield and the threats posed by military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang.

recentItems.title: CUT CABLES AND SINK TANKERS: Is Russia Preparing a Naval Blockade of the EU?
recentItems.description:
Nuclear threats against Britain and Poland, calls to destroy pipelines and undersea cables: Russian propaganda is openly discussing attacks on Europe. In this episode, we break down statements by Vladimir Solovyov and Igor Markov, who justify aggression against countries supporting Ukraine. How do Kremlin broadcasts normalize threats of mass destruction? Why are they inventing fake attack plans on Kaliningrad? And why are they calling for a naval and energy blockade of Europe? We show how Russian state media spreads fear, fabricates enemy narratives, and presents strikes on critical infrastructure as an acceptable means of leverage over the West.
